our_argument_summary: WIN-045 argues M2 (12.42h) is a trivial arithmetic consequence of the dome taking the 24.84h lunar circuit as input (LUNAR_H/2 = 24.84/2 in monitor.py, verified 2026-04-25). The deeper geometric argument: a moon at 2,534 km altitude over a 20,015 km disc produces a sharp single-spike tidal forcing field (9.24% of peak at 5,000 km offset, 0.56% at 14,000 km, 0.20% at the disc edge), contradicting the observed global two-bulge semidiurnal pattern with two roughly equal high tides per day. Post-hoc structural rebuttal invokes Part 3.1b (trivial-transcription test) and the dome author's own definition of prospective prediction. Verdict Self-Contradicted holds on either the geometric or the post-hoc argument.

holes_found.description: Cross-WIN citation-style asymmetry (new since c4). After ISS-2861 (fixed 2026-06-19, WIN-049.c5) replaced WIN-049's hedge with a dashboard-anchor citation (raw-text/08-live-power.txt lines 216-218), the three hardcoded-monitoring tidal WINs converged on two distinct citation patterns: WIN-046 cites the dome-published dashboard at raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 240 (S2), WIN-049 cites raw-text/08-live-power.txt lines 216-218 (K1), and WIN-045 alone cites an INTERNAL review artifact — the curmudgeon self-audit ('verified 2026-04-25, curmudgeon WIN-045.c4 code-tag audit'). A careful dome defender reading the three WINs side-by-side gets a free rhetorical point: two of the three cite the dome author's OWN dashboard as evidence the values are static; one cites the reviewers' OWN audit. The self-citation reads circular even when the underlying fact is identical. WIN-045 stands alone because ISS-1855 (fixed 2026-05-05) landed BEFORE ISS-2861 (fixed 2026-06-19) established the dashboard-anchor pattern. This is a discovery-only-in-hindsight issue that no c4 review could have flagged.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a parallel dome-source citation to WIN-045 detail_verdict_text without removing the audit-artifact citation. Suggested minimal edit: change the citation clause from '(verified 2026-04-25, curmudgeon WIN-045.c4 code-tag audit)' to '(the published dashboard registers M2 with Predicted: 12.42 h | Observed: 12.4206 h | Tolerance: 0.1% at raw-text/08-live-power.txt lines 212-213, and this was independently confirmed by a monitor.py source-code audit on 2026-04-25, curmudgeon WIN-045.c4 code-tag audit)'. This gives WIN-045 a dashboard-anchor primary citation matching WIN-046/049 style, while preserving the audit artifact as reinforcement. It is strictly a rhetorical strengthening, not a factual change.

holes_found.description: Awkward residual phrasing after ISS-1855 patch. The current detail_verdict_text says 'both the predicted value (LUNAR_H/2 = 24.84/2) and observed value (12.4206 h) are static constants with no live data fetch at runtime (verified 2026-04-25, curmudgeon WIN-045.c4 code-tag audit), making even that weaker test unverifiable'. Post-ISS-1855, the parenthetical asserts a positive audit finding (values ARE static constants — this WAS verified), but the trailing clause 'making even that weaker test unverifiable' now reads as if the audit failed to establish something. Intended meaning: the dome author's weaker prospective-prediction test cannot fire because both values are hardcoded at deployment — the AUDIT is what makes this determinate, not indeterminate. The word 'unverifiable' is doing double duty in a way that inverts on close read. This is a residue of the pre-ISS-1855 hedge language that was not fully re-flowed. WIN-046 (post-ISS-1812, no audit citation) uses cleaner language: 'a constant-equals-constant comparison whose 0.01% tolerance is below any physically meaningful measurement resolution'. WIN-049 (post-ISS-2861) mixes both patterns.
holes_found.recommendation: Minor rephrase. Suggested: replace 'making even that weaker test unverifiable: the observed value was fixed at deployment, not pulled from a live source after the fact' with 'confirming that no prospective prediction was ever made: both values were fixed at deployment as constants, not pulled from a live source after the fact'. The verdict-of-the-audit is asserted directly; the double-negative shrinks. Optional (parallel WIN-046 more tightly): also add the tolerance-below-resolution phrasing since it is genuinely applicable (M2 tolerance is 0.1% on the dashboard, which is comparable to but weaker than the 0.01% of K1/S2).

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly identifies M2 = lunar_day / 2 as a foundational arithmetic identity of any tidal model that takes the lunar day as input (data/wins.json:WIN-045.detail_evidence). This is the correct starting point for Doodson-style harmonic analysis and demonstrates basic tidal-taxonomy competence. The dome dashboard also correctly labels the source as 'NOAA CO-OPS published harmonic' (raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 214), acknowledging the value is not novel.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Recognizing taxonomy is not prediction. Any model that ingests 24.84h as lunar-day produces M2 by division; the period is the input, not an output distinguishing dome geometry from globe geometry (data/wins.json:WIN-045.detail_evidence). The discriminating outputs of a tidal theory are amplitudes, phases, and spatial patterns — on all three the dome is silent or contradicted by the equilibrium-forcing-field geometric argument, and this arithmetic tautology cannot substitute. The dome author's own dashboard entry (raw-text/08-live-power.txt lines 212-213) further confirms that the dome monitor makes no attempt at the discriminating amplitude/phase/spatial test — it simply reports 'Predicted 12.42h | Observed 12.4206h | PASS' with both sides fixed at deployment.

advocate_mode.best_defense: Fresh pass on the same c4 defense (non-Newtonian tidal forcing) and one new angle. Angle 1 (repeat of c4): a fair-minded dome defender argues our one-spike prediction bakes in Newtonian ∂g/∂r ∝ 1/r³ tidal forcing that the dome has not formally adopted; until the dome publishes its tidal forcing function we can only classify M2 as Not Demonstrated (mechanism unspecified), not Self-Contradicted (mechanism contradicted). Still rated 3/5 because we still have not preempted it in text. Angle 2 (new, weaker): a defender could argue the citation-style asymmetry between WIN-045 (self-audit) and WIN-046/049 (dashboard) is a sign the reviewer treated the three WINs unevenly — 'if you had a monitor.py audit for WIN-045, why not for its siblings? Either the audit is authoritative and asymmetric coverage is your reviewer's process gap, or you should not weight it heavily on WIN-045 either.' Rated 2/5 — it is a legitimate procedural observation but does not touch the substantive claim (either the values are hardcoded or they are not; the audit and the dashboard both say hardcoded, so the sibling coverage gap is procedural rhetorical noise, not factual weakness).
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Two preemptive edits: (a) integrate the c4-recommended Newtonian-forcing sentence per hole 2 above — converts angle-1 defense from severity-3 to severity-1 by assigning burden-of-proof correctly (the dome owes a mechanism it has never offered). (b) fix the citation-style asymmetry per hole 1 above — dissolves angle-2 defense entirely by giving WIN-045 the same dashboard-anchor citation posture as WIN-046/049.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: Post-ISS-2861 (2026-06-19) the five tidal WINs now sit in this state: WIN-045 (hardcoded, cites internal curmudgeon audit), WIN-046 (hardcoded, cites dome dashboard line 240), WIN-049 (hardcoded, cites dome dashboard lines 216-218), WIN-050 and WIN-051 (monitoring=none, cite absence of monitor.py entry — the correct posture for the none case, no asymmetry issue). The three hardcoded WINs are functionally consistent (all assert the values are hardcoded constants), but rhetorically asymmetric: two cite the dome-published dashboard as evidence; one cites the reviewers' own audit. This is the fresh finding driving hole 1. The correct fix is to bring WIN-045 into parallel with its siblings by dual-citing the dashboard artifact — not to strip the audit citation from WIN-045, which is genuinely additional evidence.

deeper_analysis:
Cycle 5 is a spot-check triggered by dispatcher-state recommendation Priority 5 (no work in priorities 1-4, drift-audit fresh but empty, no pending holistic checks). WIN-045 was the least-recently-reviewed WIN in the corpus (last c4 on 2026-05-05, 83 days ago).

The c4 moderate hole (internal contradiction between hedge clause and audit artifact) was cleanly closed by ISS-1855 (fixed 2026-05-05T17:20Z, verified 2026-05-05T19:05Z). The current detail_verdict_text correctly cites the audit as 'verified 2026-04-25, curmudgeon WIN-045.c4 code-tag audit'.

Two new findings emerge from the extended dormancy: (1) Cross-WIN citation-style asymmetry — after ISS-2861 (2026-06-19) landed WIN-049.c5 with a dashboard-anchor citation matching WIN-046, WIN-045 became the only hardcoded-monitoring tidal WIN citing an internal audit rather than the dome-published dashboard. This is a post-hoc rhetorical asymmetry no earlier review could have flagged because the pattern only crystallized 45 days after c4. (2) The c4 advocate_mode preemptive recommendation (add a sentence naming the non-Newtonian tidal forcing escape route) was never converted into an ISS or applied as a patch. Grep of detail_evidence for Newton/inverse-cube/aetheric coupling/aetheric tidal/forcing law/non-Newtonian returns zero matches. This is a c4-c5 handoff gap: c4 filed the recommendation under advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation rather than holes_found, and the decider does not appear to have converted it into an issue. The advocate-mode defense remains rated 3/5.

A minor cosmetic hole (awkward residual phrasing after ISS-1855 patch, hole 3) is the third finding — the trailing 'making even that weaker test unverifiable' now reads awkwardly against the confident audit citation that precedes it.

All quantitative claims verified within rounding (matches c4 numbers exactly).

Verdict Self-Contradicted holds unchanged and is robust on either the geometric argument (7.96x distance ratio, ~0.2-0.6% far-side forcing, no far-side bulge) or the post-hoc structural argument (hardcoded constants both in monitor.py and on dashboard, no prospective prediction ever made). Confidence 0.92, essentially unchanged from c4 (0.93) — the minor drop reflects one extra unpreempted advocate defense that would go to 0.94-0.95 once holes 1 and 2 are patched.

summary_for_decider: Spot-check c5 on WIN-045 (least-recently-reviewed WIN, 83 days since c4). Verdict robust; two moderate rhetorical-strengthening findings + one minor cosmetic phrasing residue. Hole 1 (cross-WIN citation-style asymmetry vs WIN-046/049) is a post-hoc discovery only visible after ISS-2861 (2026-06-19) established the dashboard-anchor pattern; suggested minimal patch preserves the audit citation while adding a parallel dashboard citation. Hole 2 (c4 advocate-mode preemptive recommendation never integrated) is a c4-c5 handoff gap the decider should convert into an ISS — file with severity moderate, source WIN-045.c5.json, category text-quality. Hole 3 is a minor phrasing residue from the ISS-1855 patch; bundle with the hole-1 patch if applied, otherwise defer. Two open-questions for decider: (a) should ISS-2861-style dashboard-anchor patches be swept across ALL hardcoded-monitoring WINs proactively (systemic fix) rather than one-at-a-time as the citation gap gets discovered? (b) should the c4 advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation field become a decider-scanned surface analogous to holes_found so unpatched preemptions do not silently age out?
